summary.text: Michael Turner is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 10th Congressional District, which he has represented since 2003. A Dayton native, he was a business and real estate attorney and mayor of Dayton before entering Congress, where he sits on the Armed Services and Oversight committees and chaired the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence from 2023 to 2025.

paragraphs.text: Turner was born in Dayton, Ohio. According to his official biography, his father worked in manufacturing in Dayton and his mother taught elementary school in Huber Heights, and he attended Dayton Public Schools and graduated from Belmont High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio Northern University in 1982, a law degree from Case Western Reserve University in 1985 and an MBA from the University of Dayton in 1992, and his official biography also lists a Doctorate in Liberal Studies from Georgetown University in 2022.
He practiced law in Dayton for more than 17 years and, according to the same biography, opened his own practice specializing in real estate and corporate law in 1991.

Turner served as mayor of Dayton from 1994 to 2002. His official biography says he created Rehabarama, a public-private housing rehabilitation partnership, and established a development fund that awarded more than $19 million in grants.
He was first elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and took office in 2003.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Armed Services Committee, with its Strategic Forces and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees, and on the Oversight Committee. He was ranking member of the Intelligence Committee in 2021 and 2022 and chaired it from 2023 to 2025.

Turner was appointed chairman of the U.S. Delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in 2011 and elected president of the Assembly in December 2014; he now serves as vice-chairman of its Defense and Security Committee.
His official biography also credits him with advocating for Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, including funding for a new National Air and Space Intelligence Center.
